anomalies.obs: The two MCP2515 CAN controllers (U47 on the CAN BUS sheet, U38 on the CAN BUS continuation) are wired to identical global labels on every SPI line: SI=NET0053, SO/MISO=NET0136, CS=NET0035, SCK=NET0074 (also INT=NET0132, RESET=NET0164). Their isolated transceivers likewise share the physical bus pair CANH=NET0135 / CANL=NET0193, and both M12 connectors J13 (CAN Interface A) and J1 (CAN Interface B) carry the same NET0135/NET0193 on their CANH/CANL pins.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the board implements 'two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)'. Each controller must have its own chip-select and its own CANH/CANL pair so the two buses are electrically separate and independently addressable.

evidence.quote: U47 pins S1=NET0053, S0=NET0136, CS=NET0035, SCK=NET0074 (CAN BUS sheet); U38 pins S1=NET0053, S0=NET0136, CS=NET0035, SCK=NET0074 (CAN BUS continuation)
U16 CANH=NET0135, CANL=NET0193; U13 CANH=NET0135, CANL=NET0193; J13 and J1 both on NET0135/NET0193

anomalies.impact: With CS tied together both MCP2515 devices are selected simultaneously and both drive the shared MISO (NET0136), causing bus contention; the two transceivers also drive the same CANH/CANL pair. The intended CAN0 and CAN1 are effectively merged into a single, non-functional bus, so independent communication with the two Odrive motor-controller branches is lost.

anomalies.obs: Both SC16IS752 UART/SPI expander chips (U8 and U10) are tied to the same global labels A0/CS=NET0169, A1/SI=NET0201, SD=NET0093, SCL/SCLK=NET0049, i.e. their chip-selects and MISO are shared.
anomalies.expected: Two SPI peripherals on one bus require separate chip-selects (and only one device driving MISO at a time); sharing A0/CS and SD between U8 and U10 merges the two serial interfaces.

evidence.quote: U8 pins A0/CS=NET0169, A1/SI=NET0201, SD=NET0093, SCL/SCLK=NET0049; U10 pins A0/CS=NET0169, A1/SI=NET0201, SD=NET0093, SCL/SCLK=NET0049 (Serial sheet)

anomalies.impact: The two UART expanders contend on the SPI MISO line and are both selected together, so the serial ports they provide cannot be addressed independently.

Reference designators differ from the spec's netlist (a build/revision difference, not flagged), but the shared-label bridging of the CAN0/CAN1 control and bus nets is a deviation from the intended two-bus architecture.
